feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear domain focus and solid public-sector experience. It shows breadth and progression well, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong progression at NACo into director-level ownership of web, analytics, governance, and multimedia.  
- Good use of scale and scope: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers” add credibility and impact.  
- Relevant, modern skill mix: Drupal, analytics stack, AI-enabled search, workflow automation, and multimedia production align well with target roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and readability.  
- Tighten bullets to emphasize outcomes over responsibilities, especially in the freelance and earlier NACo roles. Add more measurable results where possible.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; “organization-wide” vs. “organization wide” should be standardized; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is unnecessary in Education. Also standardize capitalization/style for “front-end,” date formats, and bold markdown in the footer/languages sections if plain-text CV output is intended.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning with clear seniority and domain focus. It’s slightly dense and overlaps with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience; adding one concrete scale marker would increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten phrasing and reduce list-like stacking; replace “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind” with more direct language.
- Add a concrete scale cue from recent experience (for example, 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, or 50+ publishers) to anchor credibility.
- Prioritize the most relevant themes: enterprise web modernization, governance/editorial systems, analytics, and AI-enabled discovery; multimedia can be shortened.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web modernization, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Delivers scalable digital platforms, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, and AI-enabled content experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations, including a 10,000+ page Drupal migration supporting 3.5M annual page views.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Senior digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
- The capability list closely repeats Core Competencies; keep the intro more narrative and evidence-led.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align well with the headline and recent roles, but the section is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing leadership-level capabilities will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use more concise, executive-level labels: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance & editorial operations • Analytics, reporting & insight systems • Cross-channel communications leadership
- Replace generic phrases with sharper ones: AI-enabled search & content discovery • Workflow automation & platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia, video & livestream production
- Standardize style: use either “and” or “&” consistently throughout; avoid mixing “operations,” “systems,” and “infrastructure” unless distinctions are meaningful
- Consider ordering by strongest/recentest value: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, automation, communications, multimedia

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats several ideas already stated in the header and Topline Skills, especially web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, and multimedia
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with both the summary and work experience; keep only if targeting advocacy-focused roles
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in recent roles. Tightening wording and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it feel more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use a cleaner, parallel format: “Project name: action + platform/medium + purpose/outcome.”
- Replace vague phrases like “AI-enabled” and “interactive storytelling modules” with sharper specifics tied to user value, scale, or audience.
- Standardize style and tense; e.g., use “10 x 20-foot” instead of “10×20-foot,” and keep all entries in concise past tense.
- Consider trimming to 2–3 strongest, most recent projects, especially the AI search and Drupal microsite.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series strongly overlap with the current freelance role and NACo experience bullets.
- The anniversary campaign may add the most new information because it introduces event/display work not emphasized elsewhere.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear scope and good alignment to your headline, but it reads as a task list. Tighten it around outcomes, named platforms, and 2–3 signature contributions so it feels distinct from your NACo entries.

Suggested edit
- Open with impact + client context: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4 sharper ones focused on: enterprise workflows/analytics, Drupal campaign builds, governance across channels, and AI-enabled search leadership.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, users served, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, publishing teams enabled, search accuracy/time-to-publish improvements.
- Use stronger verbs and specificity: “designed,” “implemented,” “standardized,” “launched,” “improved,” instead of “support” and “advise.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, usability and operational best practices” overlaps with NACo Director bullets; make this role more execution-heavy and current-state transformation focused.
- AI search and microsite work already appears in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and outcome-oriented.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia production, and multi-channel communications strategy.”
- Combine and streamline channel bullets; focus on scale and leadership: “Oversaw website, email, social, and video channels serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and tens of thousands of county officials.”
- Make outcomes more explicit where possible: add budget/team size, efficiency gains, engagement growth, reporting adoption, or reduced reliance on vendors for the studio build.
- Tighten wording for achievements: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page site to Drupal for 50+ internal publishers” and “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, expanding advocacy and event production capacity.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the prior Associate Communications Director role; keep this version at the strategic/enterprise level.
- Video-programming language may duplicate earlier NACo entries; emphasize studio build and organizational capacity instead.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more distinctly “operational leadership before full department ownership,” with sharper scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a clearer positioning line: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging organization-wide.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet to show build-out and repeatability: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger operations bullet: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and cross-team coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and the footer project; keep this version focused on scaling/operationalizing, not originating.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered more strongly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it largely repeats the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and outcomes-adjacent strengths rather than generic skill phrases.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive bullets:
- Enterprise digital strategy and web modernization
- Editorial governance and scalable content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership for web, email, social and video
- Public-sector and advocacy storytelling for complex stakeholder audiences
- Consider swapping “Audience-focused content planning” for “Content strategy and governance” or “Audience-centered content systems” to sound more senior and distinct.
- Keep phrasing parallel: noun-based, concise, and specific to leadership-level work.
- If space allows elsewhere, move measurable proof to recent roles rather than skills (e.g., 10,000+ page migration, 50+ publishers, 3.5M annual page views).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Advocacy and public-sector communications.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as outcome-oriented capability clusters, not a software inventory.
- Prioritize recent strengths tied to current/most recent roles: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations, automation.

items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + decision impact, e.g.:
- Analytics strategy and reporting: GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI
- User behavior and journey analysis: Microsoft Clarity, SEO and performance analysis
- KPI framework design and executive reporting
- Insight-led optimization for web, content and campaign performance
- Consider replacing “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Executive dashboards” for sharper phrasing.
- If accurate, add one measurable qualifier tied to recent work elsewhere in the CV, such as supporting a 10,000+ page site / 3.5M annual page views.
- Keep only the most differentiating tools here; move generic items like SEO to Technical + IT if space is tight.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Tool names also repeat the 2022–2024 NACo role; avoid restating the exact same list everywhere.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies. Make it more senior, operational, and tied to the studio/event capability established in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Operations**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This partly duplicates Core Competencies: **“Multimedia production and livestream operations.”** Keep one broader and one more specific.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” and “Livestreaming” are close; combine to avoid repetition.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. This item should either add specificity on level/relevance or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Add light qualifiers to show depth without overloading: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector web modernization) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, sharpen further: **Drupal 10, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats the “Topline Skills – Web Platforms & Technical Execution” entry, which already lists Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- GitHub Pages is not reinforced elsewhere and may feel lightweight beside enterprise platforms; keep only if relevant to recent consulting or portfolio work.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic keyword dump and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and newer, higher-signal tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End Development & Technical Implementation**
- Rewrite as: **HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions**
- If accurate, add scope/outcome language instead of only tools, e.g. **Front-end development for Drupal microsites and enterprise web properties; API integrations; tag deployment via GTM; edge scripting with Cloudflare Workers; CI/CD support with GitHub Actions**
- Consider dropping version numbers (**HTML5/CSS3**) unless used consistently elsewhere; **HTML/CSS** is cleaner.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution** (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations”). Keep one more strategic and this one more tool-specific.
- “Google Tag Manager” may also overlap with analytics infrastructure already covered in recent roles; include only if it reflects hands-on implementation.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already highlighted elsewhere. Make it more selective and role-relevant by emphasizing automation/build tools over general collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Project Systems**
- Reorder by strategic value and recency: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana**
- Move general collaboration tools out of this item if possible: **Slack • Teams** fit better under a broader collaboration/productivity category, or remove entirely.
- Consider adding light functional framing instead of a pure list: **Airtable systems, workflow automation, project tracking (Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills, so avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are similar; listing all four may feel padded unless each is genuinely used recently.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic software inventory. Strengthen it by signaling level of use and aligning it to the email/newsletter leadership already shown in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- If accurate, add context qualifiers: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation)** • **Higher Logic (member communications/newsletters)** • **Mailchimp (email marketing)**
- Keep naming consistent and concise; consider shortening **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys** to **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys**
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, place it first to reflect recency and depth of experience

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with work experience bullets about leading email newsletters; don’t repeat outcomes here unless you convert this into a fuller “Selected Platforms” line
- “Engagement” is broad and may duplicate “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies unless the tools are clearly email/community-specific

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” In Technical + IT, make it more tool-specific and tighten overlapping concepts.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • Optimizely/VWO (if used)**
- Swap broad terms like **SEO**, **A/B testing**, and **Dashboarding** for the actual platforms or methods used; if no named tool, use **SEO analysis** and **experiment design**.
- Order by strongest/recent tools first: **GA4, Clarity, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio** aligns with the NACo achievement and recent consulting work.
- If space allows, consider renaming to **Analytics & Optimization Tools** for clearer technical framing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially overlaps with **Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; keep Technical + IT tool-only and leave KPI/reporting language in Topline Skills.
- “Dashboarding” repeats the function already implied by **Looker Studio** and **Power BI**.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Tighten it around “built/founded early digital capacity” and only keep contributions that are distinct from later leadership roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize foundation-building: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Make the second sentence more concrete: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, expanding the organization’s in-house publishing and video capacity.”
- Replace “high-impact” with specifics or metrics if available: event audience size, video cadence, traffic lift, email growth, or production volume.
- Change “providing day-to-day guidance” to a stronger verb: “mentored” or “supervised” a digital media associate, if accurate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep it here only if this role launched the series.
- Avoid repeating workflow/governance language already covered more strongly in the 2022–2024 role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes or “firsts,” while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope + standout achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the multimedia work more specific and concise: “Produced digital and multimedia content for program communications, including planning and developing member-facing materials.”
- Elevate the strongest accomplishment: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If possible, add one measurable result: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audience/downloads, or teams/programs served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media roles; keep this item focused on innovation/research support plus the podcast first.
- Avoid broad claims about leading digital operations here, since stronger, more recent entries already cover that.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it mixes software with production capabilities and repeats multimedia themes already covered elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize tools only, with clearer senior-level relevance.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Broadcast/livestream studio production • Podcast editing & production**
- If space allows, separate tools from workflows: software first, then production capabilities.
- Consider replacing generic “Livestream studio workflows” with a stronger phrase like “Broadcast/livestream studio production” or “Studio and live event production.”
